prerequisites: Basic programming knowledge from the degree's foundational courses
Basic computer and network knowledge from the degree's foundational courses

learning_outcomes.text: Knowledge of the services and management tools that integrate an operating system.
Perform basic administration tasks of a multitasking operating system in a network environment.
Install and configure applications and services in a computer system (physical or in the cloud) to achieve the required functionality for the system.

syllabus_topics: Installation, startup, and operation of systems
Concepts of systems administration. Installation of Linux and Windows operating systems. Linux administrative tools. Windows administration console.
System startup and shutdown. Startup sequence. Linux service startup and shutdown scripts: runlevels, upstart, systemd. Linux and Windows startup troubleshooting.
Resource management and growth planning
Disks and file systems: ext3-4, NTFS. Journals. Disk administration. Partitioning. Logical volumes. Disk arrays. Partition managers. Quotas. Other storage devices.
Linux and Windows directory structure. Software installation and updates. Linux packages. System updates. Kernel modules. Windows drivers.
Backups. Backup tools. Simple backup. Multi-level backup.
User management and administration. Authentication systems
User accounts. Creation, deletion, changing properties of local users.
Local user authentication. Local groups. Resource access permissions.
Network configuration and shared resources.
Network configuration of a machine
Network authentication (LDAP, Kerberos, Active Directory)
Windows networks. Active Directory. Domains. Organizational units.
IPv6 concepts
Basic services
Firewalls: iptables, firewalls in Windows.
Network file systems: NFS and Samba/CIFS. Network backup.
Windows and Linux network services (DNS, WINS, DHCP, mail, SSH, Terminal Server, etc.)
Server migrations and basic virtualization concepts
Linux physical server migration
Windows physical server migration
Virtualization solutions
Migration of a physical server to a virtual server
Installation of operating systems and database applications.
Design and exploitation of resources
System recovery
User administration
Network configuration and basic services
Backups and scheduled tasks
Migration and virtualization
Installation and configuration of cloud systems

assessment_methods.method: Evaluation of individual or group assignments related to theory
Formative and continuous evaluation in the performance of practical work
Final evaluation of practical work (product, report, oral presentation)

assessment_rules: It is necessary to pass the theoretical and practical parts of the subject separately. If the average of theory assignments is 7 or higher, the final grade is calculated as (0.5 × Practical Grade) + (0.5 × Average Theory Assignments). If the average of theory assignments is less than 7, a theoretical exam (15% weight) is required, and the final grade is calculated as (0.5 × Practical Grade) + (0.35 × Average Theory Assignments) + (0.15 × Theoretical Exam Grade). The professor may require a videoconference after each assessment to verify knowledge.
